subject: Banking
title: Nick Leeson and Barings Bank
description: A quick win: understand Nick Leeson and Barings Bank.

hook.text: Nick Leeson lost $1.4 billion and destroyed Barings Bank in 1995. One trader sank a 233-year-old institution.

buildup.text: Leeson traded derivatives from Barings' Singapore office. He hid losses in a secret account numbered 88888.

discovery.text: Leeson doubled down on losing bets, hoping the market would recover. Each loss led to a bigger bet.

twist.text: Barings had no risk oversight in Singapore. Leeson was both the trader making bets and the manager reporting results.

climax.text: Leeson didn't start as a criminal. He hid one small loss, then another.

punchline.text: One trader. One hidden account. 233 years of banking history, destroyed.

quiz.question: What was the fundamental oversight failure at Barings?
options: Leeson was both the trader and the one reporting his own results

details.summary: Nick Leeson single-handedly destroyed Barings Bank, Britain's oldest merchant bank, by hiding $1.4 billion in unauthorized trading losses in a secret account while his superiors celebrated his apparent profits.
details.whyItMatters: The Barings collapse proved that a 233-year-old institution could be destroyed by one rogue trader. It forced the entire banking industry to rethink how it separates trading from risk oversight.
takeaways: Leeson hid losses in a secret account numbered 88888
He controlled both trading and back-office settlement functions
Barings collapsed in 1995 and was sold for one British pound

faq.question: How did Leeson hide his losses from Barings management?
faq.answer: He exploited his dual role controlling both trading and settlement. Losses were booked to a hidden error account while he reported fabricated profits to London. Management trusted the profits and never audited the account.

faq.question: What happened to Nick Leeson?
faq.answer: Leeson fled Singapore, was arrested in Germany, extradited back to Singapore, and sentenced to six and a half years in prison. He was released in 1999 and later wrote a book and became a motivational speaker.
